# 3 Axial Skyrmions
- Because the reflection flips the sign of only a single pion field, the relative phase here differs by an added π from the convention in refs. [3, 12, 7], where the antiSkyrmion is formed by reversing the sign of all three pion fields.
- The convention adopted in this work is chosen to align more naturally with the analogous monopole framework.
- As stated in (3.10), the profile function vanishes at radius s/2 from the Skyrmion (or antiSkyrmion) center, enabling a continuous gluing of the Skyrmion–antiSkyrmion pair, with the fields set to the vacuum outside their respective cores.
- Besides the basic initial data from the simple ansatz (3.7), the study also employs more refined initial conditions derived from the rational map ansatz [11] using an axially symmetric charge n map.
